title: Unexplained OOM on one no-GPU download Pod - the download transport is exonerated, cause still unknown
description:
UMBRELLA: MPI-542 - 1.4.1 field fixes (closed 2026-08-12). Members and phase order: tasks/MPI-542/brief.md.

Pod 1w58c4nmyi1jo7 (cubric-vision-pod:v0.21.0-dev-cpu, EU-RO-1, 2 vCPU / 4 GB) OOM-killed itself repeatedly on 2026-08-11 while installing MiniMax H3 Reference onto the volume. RunPod's Details tab raised 'Out of Memory (OOM) Detected'; the System log shows 'container is unhealthy: triggered memory limits (OOM)' from 17:36:47 BST, ~90s after the 17:35:13 container start, repeating every ~10s as it restarted and retried. No generation was involved.

THE ORIGINAL HYPOTHESIS IS DISPROVEN. DO NOT RE-CHASE IT. The card first blamed the hf_xet transport (MPI-491) reconstructing xorbs in memory, on the reasoning that the app showed 652 MB/s and a native Xet client decompresses and reassembles chunks across a default-16 concurrent pool. Fabio re-ran the exact install on 2026-08-11 evening and it is not that:

- Pod 3e1dd3k9six6mk, the SAME 3.725 GiB box, pulled the SAME model at up to 735 MB/s - HIGHER than the 652 that supposedly killed the first one - and completed clean.
- RunPod Telemetry during that download read 149.5 MiB / 3.725 GiB, i.e. 3%. The transport uses ~150 MB, not gigabytes.
- Throughput oscillated 200-735 MB/s across two more model installs on the same Pod with no OOM.

So the download path is exonerated and the real consumer on 1w58c4nmyi1jo7 was never identified. Nor was it the app pushing work at the Pod: the app log shows MPI-539's abandon path firing by name at 16:42, which means the getEngine fix was already live in that session and no hot-store staging could have run.

WHAT IS STILL UNKNOWN: what allocated 3.7 GB on that one Pod. The container log - the only place that would say which transport ran and what it printed - was never captured before the Pod was deleted, and the Pod is long gone.

REOPEN CRITERIA, not a plan: this stays parked unless a download Pod OOMs again. If it does, capture the CONTAINER log tab (not System, which only carries RunPod's own OOM warnings) and the Telemetry memory curve BEFORE stopping the Pod. Three healthy runs at up to 735 MB/s on a 4 GB box mean this is not a reproducible property of the download path, so speculative hardening - capping HF_XET_NUM_CONCURRENT_RANGE_GETS, or moving to a bigger box - would be a fix for a cause nobody has evidence for.

SIBLING REPO if it ever is actioned: c:/AI/Mpi/mpi-ci/cubric-vision-pod/wrapper/wrapper.py (the env block at ~line 2008 already sets HF_XET_CHUNK_CACHE_SIZE_BYTES=0 and deliberately leaves HF_XET_HIGH_PERFORMANCE unset) and start-cpu.sh. Both are R2-floated, so a change needs publish-runtime.sh, not an image rebuild.
